description: Fundamentals of music theory including notation, scales, harmony, and rhythm

notes_and_pitch.chromatic_scale: 12 semitones: C, C#, D, D#, E, F, F#, G, G#, A, A#, B
notes_and_pitch.octave: Interval spanning 12 semitones; frequency doubles each octave

scales.major_scale: Whole, Whole, Half, Whole, Whole, Whole, Half intervals; bright, happy sound
scales.natural_minor: W, H, W, W, H, W, W; darker, sadder sound
scales.pentatonic_major: 5-note scale; 1, 2, 3, 5, 6; used in folk and blues
scales.blues_scale: Pentatonic minor plus flat 5th; basis of blues music

modes.Dorian: Minor with raised 6th; used in jazz and rock
modes.Mixolydian: Major with flattened 7th; rock and blues

chords.dominant_7th: Major chord + minor 7th; creates strong pull to tonic
chords.sus2_sus4: Replace 3rd with 2nd or 4th; ambiguous, modern sound

harmony_and_progressions.key: Set of notes organized around a tonic (home note)
harmony_and_progressions.tonic: I chord; home; sense of rest
harmony_and_progressions.dominant: V chord; tension; strong pull back to tonic
harmony_and_progressions.subdominant: IV chord; soft departure from tonic

rhythm.tempo: Speed of music in BPM (beats per minute)
rhythm.time_signature: Beats per bar over note value (4/4 most common)

notation.treble_clef: G clef; lines: EGBDF, spaces: FACE
notation.bass_clef: F clef; lines: GBDFA, spaces: ACEG

musical_forms.rondo: Main theme alternates with contrasting episodes
musical_forms.fugue: Contrapuntal form; theme imitated across voices
